newsitem.title: USA: Lilly, Neurocrine say in $74-mln R&D pact.
newsitem.headline: Lilly, Neurocrine say in $74-mln R&D pact.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co and Neurocrine Biosciences Inc said they entered into a $74-million agreement to discover and develop certain compounds to treat obesity and dementia, such as that associated with Alzheimer's disease.
The agreement covers research into corticotropin-releasing factor-binding protein ligand inhibitors.

The agreement is valued at up to $74 million, provided that marketable products result, and includes sharing of technologies between the companies; funding for research, clinical development and milestones reached; and royalties on sales from any products resulting, the companies said.

Under the terms of the agreement Neurocrine would expect to receive $22 million in initial fees and research and development funding. It also also may get milestone payments based upon attainment of certain accomplishments, they said.
